text.p: Thong & Kay Hian said it has upgraded its rating on utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd to accumulate from long-term buy based on the stock's attractive valuation and expected strong operational earnings growth.

In a report issued on Monday, the brokerage firm said that based on Friday's closing price of 9.60 ringgit and lowered earnings forecasts, Tenaga is trading at prospective price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios of 66.7 times, 17.7 times and 14.1 times for financial years 1997, 1998 and 1999, respectively.
The high P/E figure for 1997 reflects lower estimated earnings after Tenaga said it anticipates foreign exchange losses from offshore loans as a result of the ringgit's weakness.
Thong & Kay Hian said it anticipated the foreign exchange translation loss to be "non-operational" and "one-off".
It estimates the electric utility could have a foreign exchange translation loss of about 680 million ringgit in fiscal year 1997, which ends in August.

Because of the expected foreign exchange loss, Thong & Kay Hian said it has reduced its estimate for financial year 1997 to 446 million ringgit from 1.126 billion ringgit for Tenaga's net profit or to 14.4 cents from 36.5 cents a share. "...we see the current weak sentiment on the TNB as an opportunity to accumulate the stock," the brokerage firm said in its report.
Tenaga's shares were down 35 cents to 9.25 ringgit in Monday afternoon trading.
